# P6 legacy behavior comparison

`inputs.json` contains nine named cases with identical rules and ordered HTTP
responses used for both the Rust adapters at `66ac372` and the new bundled Lua
adapters. They cover PatchMoe index/form requests, generic tables, Kagura CN
index/detail/category, Kagura EN multi-root index/recorded detail, and HGamer
game/patch facts including a same-column Steam widget.

Before retiring the Rust modules, both implementations were run against these
inputs and compared successfully. `expected.json` freezes that legacy result
and each HTTP URL/method/body; it is not regenerated by the current tests.
`builtin_script_migration.rs` now calls only the production source dispatcher.
Candidate IDs, candidate fingerprints, optional parser fingerprints and
observation timestamps are removed before comparison: parser identity changes
are intentional, and wall-clock observations are not website facts. Titles,
aliases, identities, variants, mirrors, completeness and request order remain.

These are reduced/synthetic offline responses, with recorded Kagura EN sections
referenced from the P0 fixtures. Passing them does not establish current live
site correctness. The ignored `builtin_scripts_live` and `hgamer_live` tests
separately exercise read-only real network metadata, without patch downloads.
